title: Mini JSON Virtual Tree Host Reconciler
problemStatement: Implement `createMiniReconciler()` with `createInstance(type, props)`, `createTextInstance(text)`, and `appendChild(parent, child)` producing a pure JavaScript object tree representing the host structure.
interviewTrap: React separates the reconciliation algorithm (reconciler) from the host mutation operations (renderer). This abstraction powers React Native, React Three Fiber, and Ink.

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: React Reconciler is platform-agnostic. By defining a Host Config object with methods like createInstance, createTextInstance, and appendChild, React can render to Canvas, Three.js, PDF, or Terminal.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Host Config Interface: createInstance & appendChild.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Fiber, Host Config Interface: createInstance & appendChild maintains state across work-in-progress trees and lanes scheduling priority.

complexity.time: O(1) per hook / O(N) fiber traversal

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is react-reconciler and what are the essential HostConfig methods?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `react-reconciler` is the core package that powers ReactDOM, React Native, and React Three Fiber. To create a custom renderer, you supply a `HostConfig` implementing host environment methods: `createInstance(type, props)` (creates host element), `createTextInstance(text)`, `appendChild(parent, child)`, `removeChild(parent, child)`, `insertBefore(parent, child, before)`, and `commitUpdate(instance, updatePayload)`.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of how React decouples reconciliation from host platform rendering.

realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: const reconciler = ReactReconciler({ createInstance(type) { return new THREE[type](); } });

realWorldUseCases.description: Rendering React components into interactive command line terminal output using ANSI escape sequences.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: import { render, Text } from 'ink'; render(<Text color='green'>Hello CLI</Text>);

howToExplain.opening: react-reconciler decouples declarative React component diffing from host platform rendering via a pluggable HostConfig interface.
keyPoints: HostConfig bridges React Fiber to any platform (DOM, WebGL, Terminal, Mobile).
appendChild and removeChild manage physical tree structure.
commitUpdate applies prop changes during the commit phase.
howToExplain.closingImpression: React is not a DOM library; React is a reconciliation engine that can render to any platform.
analogies: A universal adapter: React Fiber is the standard power outlet; HostConfig is the adapter plug that converts it to US, UK, or European sockets.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming ReactDOM is where React's diffing algorithm lives.
commonMistakes.why: ReactDOM is just a thin HostConfig wrapper around react-reconciler.
commonMistakes.correct: Clarify that react-reconciler contains the diffing engine; ReactDOM only handles browser DOM mutations.

followUpDeepDive.question: What is supportsMutation vs supportsPersistence in HostConfig?
followUpDeepDive.answer: `supportsMutation: true` indicates a mutable host tree (like browser DOM where nodes are mutated in place). `supportsPersistence: true` indicates an immutable host tree (where trees are cloned on every change, like some graphics renderers).
